title: Influcoder: Distilling Decoders' Gradient Influence Rankings into an Encoder for Data Attribution
abstract: With the growth of LLMs' (Large Language Models) capabilities, there has been an increasing push to curate high quality datasets by filtering samples in the training data. In general, Data Attribution (DA) methods aim to estimate how individual samples in a training dataset can precondition a model to generate certain outputs. As an example, one might be interested in which samples in the data could be the source of toxic behavior after training the LLM. Many methods quantify this conditioning through the paradigm of influence functions. While methods of this family are effective in its function, they lack the necessary processing speed and storage compactness to be practically implemented on large datasets. We propose a method, Influcoder, as a quick and cost-effective approach to influence-based Data Attribution at scale.

significance.justification: The paper addresses a practical bottleneck in data attribution methods by providing a faster, more scalable approach to identifying influential training samples, which directly impacts how builders curate datasets for LLM training.

novelty.justification: While building on established influence function methods, the approach of distilling decoder gradients into an encoder represents a clear technical innovation within this well-trodden research area.

reproducibility.justification: The abstract describes the high-level approach but lacks specific details about implementation, code availability, or dataset information needed for straightforward reproduction.

clarity.justification: The abstract clearly articulates the problem, limitations of existing methods, and the proposed solution's benefits, though full evaluation details are not provided.

topical_fit.justification: The paper directly addresses dataset curation and model behavior analysis, which are core concerns for builders working with LLMs in production environments.
